standards.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5.
standards.cluster: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

standards.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
standards.cluster: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

standards.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted.
standards.cluster: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

standards.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1-100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors.
standards.cluster: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

standards.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.
standards.cluster: Generate and analyze patterns.

standards.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
standards.cluster: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

standards.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols.
standards.cluster: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

standards.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
standards.cluster: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

standards.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
standards.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

standards.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations.
standards.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

standards.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division.
standards.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

standards.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size.
standards.cluster: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

standards.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as 1/2.
standards.cluster: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

standards.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.
standards.cluster: Build fractions from unit fractions.

standards.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
standards.cluster: Build fractions from unit fractions.

standards.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.
standards.cluster: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

standards.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.
standards.cluster: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

standards.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole.
standards.cluster: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

standards.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec.
standards.cluster: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements.

standards.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals.
standards.cluster: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements.

standards.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.
standards.cluster: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements.

standards.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.
standards.cluster: Represent and interpret data.

standards.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement.
standards.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

standards.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.
standards.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

standards.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts.
standards.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

standards.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.
standards.cluster: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

standards.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size.
standards.cluster: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

standards.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts.
standards.cluster: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.
